title: The Pell Cyclic Subgroup ⟨a⟩ as an Ordered Group: (ℤ, <) ≃o ⟨a⟩
description: Answers the parent entry's open question by upgrading injectivity of n ↦ aⁿ to a full isomorphism of ordered groups. For a Pell solution a with real embedding ‖a‖ = x + y√d > 1, the parent proved n ↦ R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) strictly monotone (R the regulator). This entry pulls the order of (ℝ, ≤) back along g ↦ R(g) to give the cyclic subgroup ⟨a⟩ = Subgroup.zpowers a a genuine LinearOrder (pellPowLinearOrder; injectivity of the regulator on the subgroup needs ‖a‖ > 1, since a torsion element would collapse powers), then builds the explicit order isomorphism pellPowOrderIso : ℤ ≃o ⟨a⟩ sending n ↦ aⁿ. Monotonicity in both directions is StrictMono.le_iff_le on the regulator ruler; bijectivity is the parent's zpow_injective together with the defining surjectivity of zpowers. The companion lemmas pellPowOrderIso_apply (e(n) = aⁿ), pellPowOrderIso_map_mul (e(m+n) = e(m)·e(n)) and pellPowOrderIso_map_zero (e(0) = 1) show e is simultaneously a group isomorphism, so (ℤ, +, <) ≃ (⟨a⟩, ·, ⪯) is an isomorphism of ordered groups, not merely of ordered sets. 12 theorems, 4 definitions, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The solutions of Pell's equation x² − d·y² = 1 form an infinite group, generated up to sign by a fundamental solution; the embedding (x, y) ↦ x + y√d realizes it inside the units of the real quadratic order ℤ[√d], and the logarithm of that embedding is the regulator. The grandparent chain built the regulator as an additive invariant with the linear scaling law R(aⁿ) = n·R(a); the parent pell-equation-oq-01-oq-04-oq-02 used positivity of R(a) to deduce that the powers aⁿ are pairwise distinct (injectivity of n ↦ aⁿ) and that a has infinite order. What injectivity alone does not record is the order: the cyclic subgroup ⟨a⟩ is not merely an abstract infinite cyclic group, it is an ordered group, with aᵐ ⪯ aⁿ exactly when m ≤ n. This entry makes that structure explicit.
overview.problemStatement: Upgrade the parent's injectivity of n ↦ aⁿ to a full isomorphism of ordered groups: equip the cyclic subgroup ⟨a⟩ = Subgroup.zpowers a with the order pulled back from the regulator embedding g ↦ R(g) into (ℝ, ≤), and exhibit an explicit order isomorphism (ℤ, <) ≃o (⟨a⟩, ⪯) which is simultaneously a group isomorphism — so the additive exponent line and the multiplicative cyclic subgroup are the same ordered group.
overview.proofStrategy: Three ingredients. (1) pellPowLinearOrder: the regulator g ↦ R(g) is injective on Subgroup.zpowers a when ‖a‖ > 1 — every element is aᵏ for some k, and the strictly monotone ruler k ↦ R(aᵏ) (re-proved self-contained as pellRegulator_zpow_strictMono) assigns distinct values to distinct exponents; LinearOrder.lift' transfers the order of (ℝ, ≤) back along this injection. (2) pellPowOrderIso: the equivalence n ↦ ⟨aⁿ, _⟩ has inverse g ↦ Classical.choose of its zpowers-membership witness; the left inverse is the regulator's injectivity, the right inverse is choose_spec, and map_rel_iff' is StrictMono.le_iff_le, so it is an OrderIso ℤ ≃o ⟨a⟩. (3) pellPowOrderIso_apply / _map_mul / _map_zero verify e(n) = aⁿ, e(m+n) = e(m)·e(n) and e(0) = 1, certifying e as a group isomorphism on top of the order isomorphism.
keyInsights: **The order is the regulator, made intrinsic.** The subgroup ⟨a⟩ carries no a-priori order; the strictly positive regulator supplies one by pullback. Because R is injective on ⟨a⟩ (precisely when ‖a‖ > 1), LinearOrder.lift' produces a genuine total order in which aᵐ ⪯ aⁿ ⟺ R(aᵐ) ≤ R(aⁿ) ⟺ m ≤ n.

**Injectivity was only half the story.** The parent showed n ↦ aⁿ is injective; that records the group structure of ⟨a⟩ but forgets its order. Promoting StrictMono.injective to StrictMono.le_iff_le keeps the order: the same ruler that separates powers also ranks them, turning a bijection of sets into an isomorphism of ordered groups.

**One real number determines the whole ordered group.** The regulator R(a) > 0 is the single datum: it makes ℤ, the cyclic subgroup ⟨a⟩, and the discrete subgroup R(a)·ℤ ⊂ (ℝ, +, <) all the same ordered group. The order isomorphism is the concrete witness that ⟨a⟩ ≅ ℤ as ordered groups.

**Torsion is the obstruction to the order.** The LinearOrder needs ‖a‖ > 1: if a were torsion, distinct powers would share a regulator value and the pullback would not be antisymmetric. The hypothesis enters exactly at injectivity of the regulator on the subgroup, nowhere else.

**Order iso plus group hom equals ordered-group iso.** map_rel_iff' gives the order isomorphism; pellPowOrderIso_map_mul/_map_zero give that the same map is a group homomorphism. The conjunction is the faithful statement: (ℤ, +, <) ≃ (⟨a⟩, ·, ⪯) preserves both the law and the order.

sections.title: The order isomorphism (ℤ, <) ≃o ⟨a⟩
sections.summary: pellPowOrderIso: the power map n ↦ aⁿ is an OrderIso. Bijectivity uses Subgroup.mem_zpowers_iff (surjectivity) and the regulator's injectivity (left inverse via Classical.choose); order-preservation in both directions is StrictMono.le_iff_le.

sections.title: It is also a group isomorphism
sections.summary: pellPowOrderIso_apply (e(n) = aⁿ), pellPowOrderIso_map_mul (e(m+n) = e(m)·e(n)) and pellPowOrderIso_map_zero (e(0) = 1) certify that the order isomorphism is simultaneously a group isomorphism, hence an isomorphism of ordered groups.

conclusion.summary: For a Pell solution a with real embedding ‖a‖ = x + y√d > 1, pulling the order of (ℝ, ≤) back along the regulator g ↦ R(g) gives the cyclic subgroup ⟨a⟩ = Subgroup.zpowers a a LinearOrder (pellPowLinearOrder), and the power map n ↦ aⁿ is then an explicit order isomorphism pellPowOrderIso : (ℤ, <) ≃o ⟨a⟩ that is simultaneously a group isomorphism (pellPowOrderIso_map_mul/_map_zero). This upgrades the parent's injectivity of n ↦ aⁿ to a full isomorphism of ordered groups, exhibiting ⟨a⟩ as the ordered group ℤ. 12 theorems, 4 definitions, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Identifies the cyclic subgroup generated by a Pell solution beyond 1 with the ordered group (ℤ, +, <) via the single positive number R(a): the abstract infinite cyclic group, the concrete subgroup of solutions, and the discrete lattice R(a)·ℤ ⊂ (ℝ, +) all coincide as ordered groups. The order isomorphism makes the regulator's role as a faithful, order-preserving character on ⟨a⟩ fully structural.
openQuestions: Show pellPowOrderIso is an OrderMonoidIso (a bundled order-preserving monoid isomorphism), packaging the order and group structure into a single Mathlib object rather than an OrderIso plus separate multiplicativity lemmas.

Combine with Mathlib's Pell.IsFundamental: the fundamental solution realizes the minimal positive regulator R₀, so its ⟨a⟩ is the order-isomorphic image of ℤ with the densest regulator lattice R₀·ℤ — pinning the order isomorphism that identifies a general solution's subgroup as the index-[R(a)/R₀] sublattice.

mainTheorems.name: pellPowLinearOrder
mainTheorems.statement: 0 ≤ d → 1 < pellNorm d a.x a.y → LinearOrder ↥(Subgroup.zpowers a)
mainTheorems.description: The regulator g ↦ R(g), injective on the subgroup when ‖a‖ > 1, pulls the order of (ℝ, ≤) back to a genuine LinearOrder on the cyclic subgroup ⟨a⟩ via LinearOrder.lift'.
mainTheorems.significance: Makes ⟨a⟩ an ordered set intrinsically — the order is the regulator, with torsion the sole obstruction

mainTheorems.name: pellPowOrderIso
mainTheorems.statement: 0 ≤ d → 1 < pellNorm d a.x a.y → (ℤ ≃o ↥(Subgroup.zpowers a))
mainTheorems.description: The power map n ↦ aⁿ is an explicit order isomorphism between (ℤ, <) and the cyclic subgroup with the regulator order; order-preservation is StrictMono.le_iff_le, bijectivity is surjectivity of zpowers plus the regulator's injectivity.
mainTheorems.significance: Upgrades the parent's injectivity to a full isomorphism of ordered structures — ⟨a⟩ is the ordered group ℤ

mainTheorems.name: pellPowOrderIso_map_mul
mainTheorems.statement: 0 ≤ d → 1 < pellNorm d a.x a.y → ∀ m n, e (m + n) = e m * e n
mainTheorems.description: The order isomorphism is also a group homomorphism (e(0) = 1 by pellPowOrderIso_map_zero), so (ℤ, +, <) ≃ (⟨a⟩, ·, ⪯) is an isomorphism of ordered groups, not merely of ordered sets.
mainTheorems.significance: Certifies the iso respects both the group law and the order — the full ordered-group statement

mainTheorems.name: pellPowOrderIso_apply
mainTheorems.statement: 0 ≤ d → 1 < pellNorm d a.x a.y → ∀ n, (e n : Solution₁ d) = a ^ n
mainTheorems.description: The order isomorphism is literally the power map evaluated on integer exponents.
mainTheorems.significance: Ties the abstract OrderIso to the concrete map n ↦ aⁿ
